blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Habitat loss and fragmentation is the single most critical driver forcing flora and fauna toward extinction.
Over-exploitation by human greed rather than need has led to the complete demise of species like Steller's sea cow and the passenger pigeon.
Invasive alien species disrupt local ecological balances and outcompete indigenous species for vital resources.
Co-extinction represents an indirect mechanism where the loss of a host or mutualistic partner inevitably causes the death of dependent species.

blocks.content: Habitat loss and fragmentation is the most important cause driving animals and plants to extinction.

rows: Large contiguous habitats broken into small, isolated patches affecting migratory and territorial fauna
Clearing of Amazon Rainforest ('Lungs of the Planet') for soy cultivation and cattle pasture
Harvesting rates exceeding the natural regenerative capacity of biological populations
Extinction of Steller's Sea Cow and Passenger Pigeon due to over-hunting
Introduction of non-native species turning invasive and causing decline of native fauna
Introduction of Nile Perch into Lake Victoria leading to extinction of 200+ endemic cichlid fish
Loss of one obligate species leading directly to the extinction of its dependent partner
Co-evolved plant-pollinator mutualism where extinction of one guarantees death of the other

items: The term 'Evil Quartet' refers collectively to: Habitat Loss/Fragmentation, Over-Exploitation, Alien Species Invasion, and Co-Extinction.
Parthenium (carrot grass), Lantana, and Eichhornia (water hyacinth) are key examples of invasive weed species frequently asked in UPSC examinations.
Introduction of the African catfish (Clarias gariepinus) for aquaculture poses a grave threat to indigenous catfishes in Indian rivers.
